newsitem.title: USA: Bassett sees $18.9 mln restructure charge.
newsitem.headline: Bassett sees $18.9 mln restructure charge.

text.p: Bassett Furniture Industries Inc on Wednesday said it would take a charge of $18.9 million, or $1.45 a share, in 1997 to account for the closing of its Martinsville, Virginia, plant and other restructuring moves.
Bassett Furniture said the restructuring would cut the company's annual sales by 10 percent, but the moves were expected to "significantly improve earnings."
Bassett plans to shut its promotional Impact Furniture division, eliminate its National/Mt. Airy division and move its Martinsville operations to Mount Airy, North Carolina and Bassett, Virginia.
On a pretax basis, Bassett will take a $22.4 million charge in the second quarter and $8.1 million over the remainder of the year, it said.
"Bassett is going to focus on its core Bassett line in order to improve our market share in residential home furnishings," Robert Spilman, president and chief operating officer, said in a statement.
"We will be able to offer all of our hourly W.M Bassett employees positions at our other Bassett-area plants," Spilman said, referring to employees at the W.M. Bassett facility in Martinsville.
